hook: C B S E Class Eleven Accountancy. T. S. Grewal, Question thirty-nine.
Trading account, profit and loss account, and balance sheet. All in one question.
Will the balance sheet tally? Let's solve it together.
question: Here is the question. On thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six, the following trial balance was prepared from the books of Manoj.
Debit side: opening stock, purchases, wages, salaries, machinery, furniture, building, debtors, and the expenses.
Credit side: capital, sales, bank loan, creditors, discount received, purchases return, and provision for doubtful debts.
Both sides total three lakh eighteen thousand, one hundred and sixty rupees.
Look for the stars. Every starred item has an adjustment.
adjust: One. Closing stock at cost was thirty-five thousand, whereas its net realisable value was thirty thousand.
Two. A new machine was purchased for three thousand rupees on first April, twenty twenty-five, but it was not paid for, and the entry was not recorded.
Three. Wages include five hundred rupees paid for the installation of machinery.
Four. Provision for doubtful debts was raised to one thousand four hundred, and further bad debts of three hundred were written off.
Five. Fire destroyed stock of eight thousand rupees. The insurance company admitted a claim of five thousand, paid on fifteenth April, twenty twenty-six.
Six. Outstanding wages, seven hundred. Outstanding salaries, five hundred.
Seven. Prepaid insurance, two hundred and fifty. Prepaid advertisement, five hundred.
Eight. Machinery is depreciated by ten percent, and furniture by fifteen percent.
Pause the video, and try it yourself. Then check with me.
a1: Cost, thirty-five thousand. Net realisable value, thirty thousand.
The rule: value stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower. So, thirty thousand rupees.
Closing stock is not in the trial balance, so it goes to two places.
The credit side of the trading account, thirty thousand.
And the assets side of the balance sheet, thirty thousand.
a2: Adjustments two, three and eight. The machinery.
Machinery in the trial balance, fourteen thousand six hundred.
Add the new machine, three thousand. It was bought on credit, so a creditor for machinery of three thousand goes to the liabilities side.
Add installation wages, five hundred. Installation is part of the cost of the machine, so it is capital expenditure.
Total cost of machinery, eighteen thousand one hundred.
Depreciation at ten percent. Eighteen thousand one hundred into ten, over hundred. One thousand eight hundred and ten.
Furniture. Three thousand four hundred into fifteen, over hundred. Five hundred and ten.
Total depreciation, two thousand three hundred and twenty, goes to the debit of profit and loss account.
In the balance sheet: machinery, sixteen thousand two hundred and ninety. Furniture, two thousand eight hundred and ninety.
a3: Adjustment four. Bad debts and provision.
Further bad debts, three hundred. Debtors become forty-three thousand eight hundred, minus three hundred. Forty-three thousand five hundred.
Less the new provision, one thousand four hundred. Net debtors in the balance sheet, forty-two thousand one hundred.
Now the charge to profit and loss.
Old bad debts, one thousand. Add further bad debts, three hundred. Add new provision, one thousand four hundred. That is two thousand seven hundred.
Less the old provision, eight hundred. Net charge, one thousand nine hundred rupees.
a4: Adjustment five. Loss of stock by fire.
Stock destroyed, eight thousand. This stock came from purchases, so deduct eight thousand from purchases in the trading account.
The insurance company admitted five thousand. It was received only in April, so on thirty-first March, it is an asset: insurance claim receivable, five thousand.
The balance, three thousand, is the real loss. Debit it to profit and loss account, as loss of stock by fire.
a5: Adjustments six and seven. Outstanding and prepaid expenses.
Wages. Thirty-one thousand two hundred and fifty, less installation five hundred, add outstanding seven hundred. Thirty-one thousand four hundred and fifty, to the trading account.
Salaries. Five thousand six hundred and ten, add outstanding five hundred. Six thousand one hundred and ten, to profit and loss.
Outstanding wages and salaries are liabilities in the balance sheet.
Insurance. One thousand two hundred and fifty, less prepaid two hundred and fifty. One thousand.
Advertisement. Three thousand five hundred, less prepaid five hundred. Three thousand.
Prepaid insurance and prepaid advertisement are assets in the balance sheet.
trading: Now the trading account of Manoj, for the year ended thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
To opening stock, forty thousand two hundred.

To purchases, one lakh thirty-two thousand seven hundred. Less purchases return, nine hundred and seventy. Less stock destroyed by fire, eight thousand. One lakh twenty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
To wages, thirty-one thousand four hundred and fifty.
To carriage inwards, three thousand four hundred.
Credit side. By sales, one lakh ninety-one thousand nine hundred and forty. Less sales return, one thousand two hundred and fifty. One lakh ninety thousand six hundred and ninety.
Credit total, two lakh twenty thousand six hundred and ninety.
So, gross profit is twenty-one thousand nine hundred and ten rupees.
pl: Next, the profit and loss account.
By gross profit, twenty-one thousand nine hundred and ten. By discount received, two thousand. Total, twenty-three thousand nine hundred and ten.
Debit side. Salaries, six thousand one hundred and ten. Discount allowed, two thousand six hundred and forty. Bank charges, ninety.
Bad debts and provision, one thousand nine hundred.
Insurance, one thousand. Rent, two thousand four hundred and fifty. Advertisement, three thousand.
Loss of stock by fire, three thousand.
Depreciation. Machinery, one thousand eight hundred and ten. Furniture, five hundred and ten. Total, two thousand three hundred and twenty.
Net profit, one thousand four hundred rupees.
bs: Finally, the balance sheet of Manoj, as at thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
Capital, one lakh. Add net profit, one thousand four hundred. Less drawings, four thousand two hundred. Ninety-seven thousand two hundred.
Bank loan, ten thousand. Sundry creditors, twelve thousand four hundred and fifty.
Creditor for machinery, three thousand. Outstanding wages, seven hundred. Outstanding salaries, five hundred.
Liabilities total, one lakh twenty-three thousand eight hundred and fifty.
Assets. Building, twenty-one thousand seven hundred. Machinery, sixteen thousand two hundred and ninety. Furniture, two thousand eight hundred and ninety.
Closing stock, thirty thousand. Sundry debtors, forty-two thousand one hundred.
Insurance claim receivable, five thousand. Prepaid insurance, two hundred and fifty. Prepaid advertisement, five hundred.
Cash at bank, two thousand four hundred and seventy. Cash in hand, two thousand six hundred and fifty.
Assets total, one lakh twenty-three thousand eight hundred and fifty. The balance sheet tallies!
traps: Four exam traps from this question.
Trap one. Closing stock goes at thirty thousand, the lower of cost and net realisable value. Not thirty-five thousand.
Trap two. Installation wages are added to machinery, not left in wages. So depreciation is on eighteen thousand one hundred.
Trap three. Loss by fire. Deduct the full eight thousand from purchases. Only the uninsured three thousand is a loss in profit and loss. The claim of five thousand is an asset.
Trap four. Bad debts. Deduct further bad debts and the new provision from debtors. Subtract the old provision only in profit and loss.
recap: Gross profit, twenty-one thousand nine hundred and ten.
Net profit, one thousand four hundred.
Balance sheet total, one lakh twenty-three thousand eight hundred and fifty, on both sides.
Every adjustment has two effects. Find both, and your balance sheet will tally.
